lines.text: An institution/agency [instantie] is an organization [organisatie] that can make decisions.
For example the government [overheid].
The municipality, the police, the tax office [Belastingdienst] and the UWV are institutions that belong to the government.
There are also other institutions, for example the Juridisch Loket or an insurance company [verzekeringsmaatschappij], such as your health insurer.
As a citizen [burger] in the Netherlands you have rights and duties [rechten en plichten].
For example, you have the right to a benefit, or the right to information and help with problems.
You also have duties, for example to pay taxes.
The government and other institutions must communicate with people.
You can call the municipality or the Belastingdienst, and they can send you letters.
But usually communication is digital [digitaal]: you look for information on websites, or you make an appointment digitally.
Do you have trouble with digital contact?
Then you can get help, for example at the library.
There is also a digital help line [DigiHulplijn], a phone number you can call.
Everyone who lives in the Netherlands has their own number: the citizen service number [bsn, burgerservicenummer].
It is a number with nine digits.
It appears, for example, in your passport or on papers from the Belastingdienst.
You sometimes have to fill in your bsn on forms.
For digital communication you have to prove who you are at many institutions.
You can do that with your DigiD, a kind of digital passport.
You need your DigiD when you want to log in [inloggen] at the municipality, the Belastingdienst, your health insurance, the education executive agency [DUO, Dienst Uitvoering Onderwijs] and the UWV.
You can log in with an app on your phone (the easiest way) or with a username [gebruikersnaam] and password [wachtwoord].
Everyone in the Netherlands has by law the right to privacy [recht op privacy]:
Do not give your bsn and DigiD to someone else just like that [zomaar].
Also be careful with a copy of your passport or identity card [identiteitskaart] — people can misuse your data [gegevens misbruiken], for example to make a fake [vals] passport.
You only have to give what is needed.
Your school may ask for your bsn, but not your PIN code [pincode].
Institutions must handle your personal information carefully [zorgvuldig].
You always have the right to see what information an institution has about you, for example what is in your file [dossier].
